Forwarding privacy counsel memo and my inline comments. See attached (PrivacyCounsel_Memo.pdf). Highlights from counsel (Mark Chen):

- Subprocessors: counsel recommends the 30-day notice but wants to retain a rolling "catch-up" carveout for emergency/urgently added infra providers (require notice as soon as practicable and post-notification obligation). Proposed text: "Redwood will provide at least 30 days' notice of any new subprocessor where commercially reasonable; in cases requiring immediate engagement for security, redundancy, or legal reasons Redwood will notify DataPulse as soon as practicable and remediate any concerns."
- Published list: include a requirement to maintain a historical list for 180 days so customers can audit recently used subprocessors.
- Certifications/evidence: acceptable to provide copies of the most recent SOC2 Type II and an ISO attestation; for targeted audits we propose a standard process (scope, cost allocation, NDA).
- Cross-border: propose SCC-like text plus an explicit statement that where SCCs cannot be relied on, Redwood will implement and document transfer risk assessments and appropriate technical/legal safeguards. Counsel flagged that a blanket "SCCs only" ask may be infeasible in certain cloud jurisdictions.

I've inserted inline redlines in the attached PDF and suggested fallback language. Lina — can you confirm which legal contact at DataPulse will review the fallback language?

-Neha
